categories.main_business_segments: SAN-AI OBBLI operates five main business segments: Petroleum-related (fuel sales, storage, and distribution), Chemicals (manufacturing and sales of chemical products), Gas (LP gas, natural gas, and related equipment sales), Aviation (airport fuel storage and aircraft refueling), and Other (construction, real estate leasing, metal surface treatment, and building management).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages logistics and storage infrastructure for petroleum and gas, proprietary chemical formulation and manufacturing (including car care chemicals and anti-corrosion agents), advanced safety and operational systems for airport fueling, and specialized technologies for metal surface treatment and precision cleaning (notably for semiconductor equipment). Digital transformation (DX), ERP, and automation are increasingly integrated into operations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include industrial and commercial fuel users, automotive service providers, gas retailers and end-users (households and businesses), airlines and airport operators, and manufacturers requiring specialty chemicals or precision cleaning. The company serves both B2B and B2C markets, with a strong presence in energy, transportation, and industrial sectors.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are primarily domestic, with a nationwide footprint across Japan. Key regions include Kanto, Tokai, Kinki, Chugoku, and Kyushu, with major assets in Tokyo, Haneda Airport, and regional gas and fuel distribution centers. There is no significant overseas business or assets.
categories.supply_chain_position: SAN-AI OBBLI operates mainly in the midstream and downstream segments: it procures petroleum and gas from upstream suppliers, manages storage and logistics, and distributes to wholesalers, retailers, and end-users. In chemicals, it is both a manufacturer and distributor. In aviation, it provides critical infrastructure and services at airports.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company is executing a mid-term plan focused on transforming its portfolio toward low-carbon and circular economy solutions, expanding growth areas (chemicals, gas, clean tech), and strengthening digitalization (DX) and operational efficiency. R&D is directed at functional chemicals, high-value specialty products, and advanced cleaning technologies, with investments in new plants and digital platforms. There is a strong emphasis on sustainability, decarbonization, and business model innovation.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through product sales (petroleum, gas, chemicals), service fees (airport fueling, construction, cleaning), and real estate leasing. The company also earns from wholesale and retail distribution, as well as facility management and maintenance contracts.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other Japanese energy distributors, gas companies, and chemical manufacturers such as ENEOS, Idemitsu, and Cosmo Energy. SAN-AI OBBLI is a leading independent player with a diversified portfolio, strong regional networks, and a focus on both traditional and emerging energy/chemical markets. It is positioned as a stable, mid-sized group with a reputation for reliability and innovation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For FY2025, consolidated sales were ¥654.4 billion, with operating profit of ¥11.8 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥8.7 billion. The company has over 1,800 employees and maintains a solid balance sheet (equity ratio ~55%). While overall sales are stable, profit declined in FY2025 due to margin pressures and impairment losses; growth is targeted in chemicals, gas, and clean tech, with ongoing portfolio transformation.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: SAN-AI OBBLI emphasizes reliability in energy supply, comprehensive nationwide logistics, and safety in hazardous materials handling. Its differentiation lies in integrated solutions across petroleum, gas, chemicals, and aviation fueling, as well as its commitment to sustainability, digital transformation, and customer-centric innovation. The company is also investing in next-generation energy and clean tech, aiming to support customers' transition to a low-carbon future.
